En el plano, un punto necesitaba dos núm: In the plane, a point needed two numbers. In space it needs three: how far forwards, how far to the right and how far up. Everything you learnt with [[ge-vectores|vectors in the plane]] still holds with one more coordinate, and two new operations appear — the cross product and the scalar triple product — which are worked out with the [[al-determinantes|determinants]] from the algebra block and which turn the geometry of space into something calculated rather than something imagined.
Este tema es la caja de herramientas de: This topic is the toolbox for the next two. With the three products here you write the equations of lines and planes, measure angles and distances and work out areas and volumes. It pays to master it before going on: in the exam, almost every geometry slip is a slip in these calculations.

Una <strong>combinación lineal</strong>: A linear combination of $\vec{u}$ and $\vec{v}$ is any vector of the form $\lambda\vec{u} + \mu\vec{v}$, with $\lambda$ and $\mu$ numbers. If one of the vectors in a list can be written as a combination of the others, it is redundant: they are said to be linearly dependent. If none is redundant, they are independent.
En el espacio eso tiene una lectura geom: In space that has a very clean geometric reading:
<strong>Dos</strong> vectores son depend: Two vectors are dependent when they are parallel: one is a multiple of the other, and their coordinates are proportional.
<strong>Tres</strong> vectores son depen: Three vectors are dependent when they are coplanar: all three fit in the same plane.
<strong>Cuatro</strong> vectores del esp: Four vectors in space are always dependent: there is no room for a fourth independent one.
Tres vectores independientes forman una: Three independent vectors form a basis of $\mathbb{R}^3$: any other vector is written, in one way only, as a combination of them. The most convenient is the standard basis $\vec{\imath} = (1,0,0)$, $\vec{\jmath} = (0,1,0)$, $\vec{k} = (0,0,1)$. And to know whether three vectors form a basis you do not have to draw anything: a [[al-determinantes|determinant]] is enough.
\\{\\vec{u}, \\vec{v}, \\vec{w}\\}\\ \\t: \{\vec{u}, \vec{v}, \vec{w}\}\ \text{is a basis} \iff \begin{vmatrix} u_1 & u_2 & u_3 \\ v_1 & v_2 & v_3 \\ w_1 & w_2 & w_3 \end{vmatrix} \ne 0

Las llaves $\\{\\ \\}$ agrupan los tres:
The braces $\{\ \}$ group the three vectors. The symbol $\iff$ is read “if and only if”.

It is said: “u, v and w form a basis if and only if the determinant with their coordinates as rows is not zero”.

Why: that determinant is the (signed) volume of the box the three form. If it is zero, the box is flattened, all three lie in a plane, and a plane is not enough to describe the whole of space.

It is the idea behind all the distances in the topic [[ge-metrico]].

Con el producto vectorial se construye a: With the cross product something very concrete is built: a camera. Given where the eye is, the point it looks at and a rough idea of where the sky is, two cross products give the three perpendicular vectors defining the view. It is set up in [[gfx-camara|the camera: a basis from the cross product]], and it is one of the places where this operation stops looking like a mnemonic.
El producto vectorial nació dentro de ot: The cross product was born inside something else. In 1843 William Rowan Hamilton invented quaternions, numbers with four components, and multiplying two of them brought out, mixed together, a dot product and a cross product. For forty years physics was written with quaternions and it was cumbersome. Around 1880 Josiah Willard Gibbs, in the United States, and Oliver Heaviside, in England, each on his own, separated the two parts and created vector calculus as it is studied today. Hamilton's supporters considered it a mutilation, and the argument in the scientific journals lasted years.

The brackets $[\vec{u},\vec{v},\vec{w}]$ are read “scalar triple product of u, v and w”, and it is worked out as the determinant of the three vectors laid out as rows.

Its absolute value is the volume of the parallelepiped. The tetrahedron with vertices $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$ takes up exactly one sixth of the parallelepiped formed by its three edges from $A$: a half for having a triangular base and a third for being a pyramid.

Cada superficie de un videojuego o de un: Every surface in a video game or an animated film is a mesh of thousands of triangles, and to light each one you have to know which way it faces: its normal, worked out with a cross product of two of its sides. The graphics card does that calculation millions of times a second. In physics, the cross product is the moment of a force — why a long spanner loosens a bolt better — and the force a magnetic field exerts on a charge, which is what makes any electric motor turn. And the scalar triple product is the calculation with which a 3D design program works out the volume, and therefore the weight, of a part before it is manufactured.
